title: ARP and ping on the lab network
description: LAB-PC-37 finds the hardware address of LAB-PC-38 with ARP, pings it four times, then tries an address no PC has.
questions: What MAC address does LAB-PC-38 have, and which company made its network card?
How long did the first ping take to come back (look at the Time column)?
Why does the PC send three ARP requests at the end, and why is there no ping after them?

title: A web page: DNS, TCP and HTTP
description: The PC looks up labs.foct.test, opens a TCP connection to port 80 and loads a page, its logo and a missing favicon.
questions: Which IP address did DNS give for labs.foct.test, and how long may the PC keep it (TTL)?
Find the three packets of the TCP handshake. Which ports do the two sides use?
Follow the HTTP stream: what status code came back for /favicon.ico?
Use Statistics > HTTP objects to save the logo the page loaded.

title: TCP: a lost segment and its retransmission
description: A download of results.csv loses one segment. The PC sends duplicate ACKs and the server sends the segment again.
questions: Which packet shows that a segment was not captured?
How many duplicate ACKs did the PC send?
What sequence number did the retransmitted segment carry?

title: DHCP: a PC gets its address
description: Discover, Offer, Request and Acknowledge, then the PC checks with ARP that nobody else uses its new address.
questions: Which IP address, subnet mask, gateway and DNS server did the PC get?
Why are the DHCP messages sent to 255.255.255.255?

title: FTP: a password in clear text
description: A student logs in to an FTP server. FTP sends everything, the password included, as plain text.
questions: Follow the TCP stream: what user name and password were sent?
Why should a lab use SFTP or FTPS instead of FTP?

title: HTTPS: what TLS keeps private
description: The PC opens an HTTPS connection with TLS 1.3. The server name is visible in the Client Hello; the page itself is encrypted.
questions: Which server name (SNI) did the PC ask for?
Which cipher suite did the server choose?
Can you read the page or the request? Compare with the HTTP and FTP captures.
